bib.title: A Contextual-Bandit Approach to Personalized News Article Recommendation

question: How can personalized news article recommendation with a changing article pool be done with a contextual bandit, and how can such a bandit be evaluated offline without bias?
hypothesis: Feature-based UCB exploration (LinUCB) beats context-free and epsilon-greedy bandits, especially when data is sparse; hybrid models speed learning by sharing features across arms.
contributions: A new general contextual bandit algorithm, LinUCB, computationally efficient and motivated by learning theory
An argument that any bandit algorithm can be reliably evaluated offline using previously recorded random traffic
Application of LinUCB to a Yahoo! Front Page Today Module dataset of over 33 million events, with a 12.5% click lift over a standard context-free bandit

method.summary: LinUCB fits a ridge regression per arm (disjoint) or with shared coefficients (hybrid) and picks the arm with highest upper confidence bound. Algorithms are scored offline with a replay (rejection-sampling) evaluator on events logged under uniform random article choice from Yahoo! Today Module, May 2009.
method.task: personalized news article recommendation as a K-armed contextual bandit

datasets.name: Yahoo! Today Module random bucket, tuning day
datasets.source: Yahoo! random bucket; articles chosen uniformly at random; only F1 article at story position used
datasets.preprocessing: user features: support >= 0.1, over 1000 categorical components encoded as binary, unit-length normalised, plus constant 1 (1193 entries); article features 83 entries

datasets.name: Yahoo! Today Module random bucket, evaluation week
datasets.preprocessing: 6-dim features: logistic-regression bilinear model, user features projected, K-means into 5 clusters, soft membership (Gaussian kernel, normalised) plus constant 1; hybrid z = outer product of user and article 6-dim features = 36 dims

datasets.name: Random exploration data, Sept 2008
datasets.preprocessing: used for conjoint analysis/dimension reduction and to train the warm-start bilinear LR model

other.complexity: O(d^2+k^2) per trial with cached inverses

models.name: epsilon-greedy, ucb (UCB1, c=alpha/sqrt(n)), omniscient, random, warm-start and seg variants, epsilon-greedy disjoint/hybrid

training.objective: online ridge regression on click payoff (0/1)

other.tuned_values: epsilon and alpha tuned on the one-day tuning data; chosen values are only in Figure 2, not in the text

inference.samples: one run per algorithm on evaluation data; data sparsity levels 100, 30, 20, 10, 5, 1% by random subsampling of data the algorithm learns from (all data still used for evaluation)

parameters.alpha: LinUCB theory value 1+sqrt(ln(2/delta)/2); tuned empirically, value not printed
parameters.epsilon: epsilon-greedy parameter, tuned, value not printed

metrics.name: relative CTR
metrics.definition: clicks / steps run, divided by the random policy's CTR, estimated with Algorithm 3 (policy evaluator) on random logged events

eval.protocol: Replay evaluator: step through logged uniform-random events, keep an event when policy chooses the logged arm; unbiased by Theorem 1, expected K*T events needed. Two CTRs: learning bucket (small traffic fraction running the bandit) and deployment bucket (greedy serving from learned estimates). Single run, no significance test; authors argue size of data makes numbers reliable.

availability.data: Proprietary Yahoo! logs; CTRs reported only relative to random for business confidentiality

results.claim: The replay evaluator is unbiased and needs K*T logged events in expectation to retain T events.
results.setup: Uniform random logging policy, i.i.d. events (Theorem 1)
results.note: Proof given; weaker (any randomised logging) case said to need rejection sampling at lower efficiency, details omitted.

limits: Logging policy must be uniform random and events i.i.d.; the generalisation to other randomised logging is stated but details omitted.
Single run per setting, no confidence intervals; tuned alpha and epsilon values not printed in text.
Absolute CTRs withheld; only relative to random, and data is proprietary.
Hybrid derivation deferred to a full paper; regret bound O~(sqrt(KdT)) is claimed adapted from Auer, not proved here.
Only 6-dim cluster features tested; authors say more diverse features would be needed to separate linucb (disjoint) from ucb (seg).
Warm-start variants tuned but dropped from evaluation week because they did not beat online learners on tuning data.
Ignores user interests changing over time (future work).

terms.definition: A learning algorithm sequentially selects articles to serve users based on contextual information about the users and articles, while adapting to click feedback.
Algorithm 3: retain a logged event only if the evaluated policy picks the logged arm; unbiased when logging is uniform random.
